speaker: will_kemp
text: A holiday yard, and you with a face as long as the tale. Was the rope in earnest this time?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It is never in earnest. The yard was. Two of the clock, and full.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Thou stood'st like a man counting the boards. The cold, or the length of it?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The tale is long, and I have said it since Christmas. The cold is the parlour. I am well.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Well is a fine word. You had a speech at each end and a stool in the middle, and you may keep the word.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Leave him, Kemp. Holywell is after this, and my mother has a cake that will not wait on a joke.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: If the bean finds Nick, he will be grave. I am not writing him a speech for it.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Do not write me a silence either. I have heard there is to be a king, and I intend to talk.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Come, Will. The yard is out. Thou wilt want the walk, not another proverb.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am coming. Give me the cloak.
